tasks.title: Scoped durable source import backend
steps: Create internal/acquisition service and PostgreSQL migration 073 using shippin_ tables: source registration with immutable source tenant/project/issuer/audience, source ID, config generation, cursor and pause state; sealed source credentials and sealed per-source lead payloads keyed by immutable source/lead ID and revision. Add acquisition.read and acquisition.sync to permission catalog, sync marked high-risk and both explicitly grantable. Grant owner preset only, including migration and fresh owner seed as appropriate. Ensure development account auto-grants do not implicitly gain either permission.

Implement narrow generated MCPL staff actions under internal/tenancy/acquisition_source: list/create/update/sync and nested lead/list. List sources under acquisition.read returns safe metadata only. Lead list uses acquisition.read. Create/update uses platform.settings.write; inputs validated, secrets write-only; updates increment config generation and explicitly pause/resume. Sync uses acquisition.sync; output only aggregate count/cursor/more, never email. No source identity rewrite, cursor reset or source deletion workflow in this slice. Root owns generated artifacts coordination and UI; agree output structs before integration.

Wire lazy platform sealing through internal/api/acquisition_services.go and provideServices in internal/api/mcpl_services.go. Use a.sealer() with distinct stable AAD bound to acquisition source ID plus kind and lead ID; fail closed if no key. Seal signer and lead payloads, never store bearer JWT. Read-only list returns only unexpired entries, decryption failures fail closed; never log secret, bearer, URL query, raw response, email, or decrypted values. Existing session key rotation renders sealed content unavailable and is a documented recovery risk.

Implement a narrowly validated source v1 HTTP client in internal/acquisition. Source origin must be HTTPS without userinfo, path/query/fragment; dial an explicitly configured numeric IP and port with proxy disabled, no DNS, original TLS server name and explicitly configured CA, no redirects, bounded timeouts and response bytes. Reject unspecified/multicast/link-local and cloud metadata destinations; allow an explicitly configured loopback or private address. Validate TLS hostname and certificate, then mint a 120-second Ed25519 JWT server-side from encrypted signer per request for exact issuer/audience/tenant/project and only marketing:read, never expose key or token. Endpoint and key trust are security-review prerequisites, not production identity proof.

Fetch at most one bounded page per manual sync. Validate version=1, retention 1..730, maximum 1 MiB and 100 records, 32-hex IDs, monotonically increasing revisions, cursor equality to last item, timestamp/consent/status constraints, and tombstones without PII while permitting zero timestamps. Decrypt/sign and perform network call with no source row lock held. Because MCPL begins a write transaction before Run, fetch occurs within that open transaction with strict timeout; after fetch acquire row lock or compare-and-swap expected cursor+generation+unpaused state. Apply all records, source-scoped dedup and cursor in the same c.DB transaction and let MCPL atomically audit/commit. A failed CAS or any item failure applies nothing. Reject stale config and concurrent competing pages; tombstones clear ciphertext and record revision floor.

Read filters expiry on every request. Add context-bound console lifecycle RunAcquisitionRetention analogous to RunSweeper: immediate then periodic bounded idempotent deletion of expired sealed lead payloads, independent of source availability, safe across replicas, stop on cancellation and log sanitized failures. Keep enough source-scoped deletion suppression/revision floors for the reviewed reconciliation policy; never claim physical purge while platform process is stopped. Tests must prove expiration after a source outage and startup purge.

Source v1 has no epoch, high-water mark or scope identity: never infer restore from an empty page and never silently reset cursor or unpause. An operator who knows source was restored must pause/quarantine it; stale in-flight requests fail generation CAS. Reconciliation/reset and durable replay suppression beyond this bounded initial slice remain explicit security-review follow-up; do not implement a blind reset or claim automatic restore detection.

Run focused Go tests and generation; use explicitly disposable synthetic Postgres/TLS/source credentials. Negative tests include anonymous/customer/nonstaff/inactive/wrong permission and wrong project; no real service access, no provisioning. Coordinate UI contract and cross-process integration with root. Stop if lifecycle wiring, sealer, generator, trust or role semantics contradict these anchors.

checks.expected: Pass all applicable focused backend tests; explicitly report opt-in skips.
Regenerate registry, typed action map and OpenAPI consistently.

acceptance: Only explicitly authorized staff can configure, sync or view; no accidental ordinary or dev-account grants.
Source pages are atomically applied with cursor/config-generation CAS and audit, encrypted PII, deduplication, deletion and independent expiry.
Synthetic private TLS and real disposable PostgreSQL tests establish actual storage/retry/error behavior, or limitations remain open.
No production identity, public deployment, live provider, browser end-to-end, or automatic restore safety is claimed.

escalation_triggers: Source anchors or baseline change before dispatch.
Permission, signer, sealing, retention, SSRF, restoration, consent or authorization ambiguity.
Requested live access, provisioning or cross-repository implementation.
Lifecycle ownership or generated-action contract cannot be met within authorized files.
